3619	[00:23:53] Deniz Arı: Silence: first two times, short repeat of the question. Third time "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and the call is closed.
3620	[00:24:02] Deniz Arı: Unclear answer or refusal: ask again, three tries per question. After three: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Repeating information doesn't count.
3621	[00:24:12] Deniz Arı: Non-Turkish: "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum."
3622	[00:24:15] Deniz Arı: Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to the flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.
3623	[00:24:26] Deniz Arı: Card selection: same name, last four. Same last four: "Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?" Same last six: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
3624	[00:24:42] Selin Aydın: With the real digits, not 4253.
3625	[00:24:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, of course, from the service.
3626	[00:24:46] Deniz Arı: Angry customer: up to three calming replies, then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." No reaction to insults.
3627	[00:24:53] Deniz Arı: Currency names always in full, Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini, also in the no-debt sentence.
3628	[00:25:00] Deniz Arı: Statement week: once per calendar year. Not offered if the right is used. Mentioning the limit is optional. Kerem checks the pre-check service with Mert.
3629	[00:25:09] Deniz Arı: Joint statement: before the confirm question, "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek." For the linked card holder, before the confirm question, that the main card is affected too.
3630	[00:25:21] Deniz Arı: Normal end, nothing else wanted: "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now, to look at again with the routing project.
3631	[00:25:28] Elçin Ural: One correction. For the joint statement, not only "before confirming". Before the question. I want the customer to hear it, and then the question comes.
3632	[00:25:35] Deniz Arı: Yes, that's what I meant. Sentence first, then "Onaylıyor musunuz?".
3633	[00:25:39] Elçin Ural: Okay.
3634	[00:25:40] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Selin, you'll fix the document?
3635	[00:25:43] Selin Aydın: I'll fix what I can by tomorrow. The edge case section I'll redo anyway, it's a mess.
3636	[00:25:51] Deniz Arı: I'll send it, maybe not today, tomorrow or Friday.
3637	[00:25:54] Selin Aydın: Fine.
3638	[00:25:55] Burcu Tan: And I'll send the silence timing from the IVR. And I'll fix my prompts for the yearly limit, but that's for the IVR, not for you.
3639	[00:26:02] Ozan Er: Thanks Burcu.
3640	[00:26:04] Kerem Yalçın: Anything else? The [inaudible] mobile app topic we do next week, not today.
3641	[00:26:09] Selin Aydın: Next week, yes. Ah, and Elçin, mandatory texts, is there anything the assistant must say at the start?
3642	[00:26:15] Elçin Ural: I'm checking. I'll write to you. I don't think so for this flow because the customer is already identified in the IVR, but let me confirm.
3643	[00:26:22] Selin Aydın: Okay, thanks.
3644	[00:26:24] Deniz Arı: One more for us, sorry, thirty seconds. When the debt service doesn't answer, an error, we go to an agent, not main menu. Still okay?
3645	[00:26:31] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Service error, agent. The customer did nothing wrong, they shouldn't land in the menu.
3646	[00:26:36] Deniz Arı: And the sentence from the mails stays, "Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
3647	[00:26:42] Kerem Yalçın: Yes.
3648	[00:26:43] Deniz Arı: Perfect, that's all from us.
3649	[00:26:45] Ozan Er: Oh, last thing, the digits. When the customer says "kırk iki elli üç" for the last four, that's the same as "dört iki beş üç", we just map it, we don't read it back.
3650	[00:26:53] Selin Aydın: Yes, any way they say it.
3651	[00:26:55] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, I really have to go. Thanks everyone, good session.
3652	[00:26:58] Burcu Tan: Bye bye.
3653	[00:26:59] Elçin Ural: Thanks, bye.
3654	[00:27:00] Selin Aydın: Bye. Deniz, Ozan, can you stay one minute?
3655	[00:27:03] Deniz Arı: Sure.
3656	[00:27:05] Selin Aydın: Is it okay for you if the document only catches up next week? I have the quarterly report this week and honestly...
3657	[00:27:11] Deniz Arı: No problem. We have our notes from today.
3658	[00:27:15] Selin Aydın: Thanks. And the six-digit comment, you'll put it?
3659	[00:27:18] Deniz Arı: Yes, right after this.
3660	[00:27:20] Ozan Er: Selin, one question about the test cards, the two Yıldız cards in the test data, do they really share the last four?
3661	[00:27:26] Selin Aydın: I think so, Mert built them for exactly that. Ask him, I'm not a hundred percent sure.
3662	[00:27:31] Ozan Er: Okay, I'll ask.
3663	[00:27:32] Selin Aydın: Okay. Thanks both. Talk Friday.
3664	[00:27:34] Deniz Arı: Thanks, bye.
3665	
3666	[recording stopped]

=== FILE: sources/meetings/2026-10-07-analysis-session-transcript.txt ===
=== META: date=2026-10-07; type=meeting note; author=unknown ===

Statement debt analysis session - Freya Bank / Freya
Wednesday 7 October 2026, 14:30, video call
Recording: automatic transcript, excerpt. Speaker detection may be wrong where people talk over each other.
Participants: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan, Elçin Ural (joined at about 00:14), Deniz Arı, Ozan Er

[...]

[00:01:12] Selin Aydın: ...okay, I think it's recording now. Kerem is in another call, he said five minutes.
[00:01:17] Burcu Tan: Then it's ten minutes [laughs].
[00:01:19] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Probably. Deniz, Ozan, can you hear me fine?
[00:01:22] Deniz Arı: Yes. Hi Selin, hi Burcu.
[00:01:24] Ozan Er: Hi. Sorry, my camera is off, the internet here is a bit weak today.
[00:01:28] Burcu Tan: Are you at the office?
[00:01:29] Ozan Er: No, at home, the building is doing something with the cables. Since Monday.
[00:01:33] Burcu Tan: Ours was like that last year, three weeks. Good luck.
[00:01:36] Selin Aydın: Okay. While we wait for Kerem, maybe two small things on the reading part? Those don't need him.
[00:01:42] Deniz Arı: Sure. We had a few small ones too.
[00:01:45] Selin Aydın: First, the order. When a card has debt in more than one currency. I wrote Türk Lirası first, then the foreign currencies. Is that clear enough in the document?
[00:01:54] Ozan Er: Mostly. We read it as: the card intro with the statement date, then Türk Lirası, then Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini in that order, then one sentence for all the currencies with no debt, then the due date.
[00:02:06] Selin Aydın: Yes, exactly that.
[00:02:08] Ozan Er: And the remaining automatic payment, if there is one, before the due date.
[00:02:12] Selin Aydın: Yes. Before the due date.
[00:02:14] Burcu Tan: The IVR reads the due date last too. People remember the last thing they hear.
[00:02:18] Deniz Arı: Makes sense.
[00:02:20] Ozan Er: Then for the due date the sentence is "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi]'dir." with the date like "21 Ekim 2025". Day, month name, year.
[00:02:30] Selin Aydın: Yes. And if the due date is today, it should say today. Not the date.
[00:02:35] Ozan Er: "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür." Okay, we have that.
[00:02:39] Selin Aydın: Good.
[00:02:41] Deniz Arı: Second small one from us. After the debt is read, if the customer has more than one card, what comes first, the other-card question or the offer? E-mail and the week change.
[00:02:51] Selin Aydın: Hm. I'd say other card first. The customer called for the debt. If they have another card, maybe they want that one too.
[00:02:58] Deniz Arı: So: "Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?" and only when the cards are done, or they say no, the offer.
[00:03:05] Selin Aydın: Yes. Let's confirm with Kerem but I think he'll agree.
[00:03:09] Burcu Tan: And if they have only one card, you don't ask the other-card question, obviously.
[00:03:13] Deniz Arı: No, then straight to the offer.
[00:03:15] Ozan Er: And the offer only has what the customer can actually do. That's why we keep asking about the e-mail and the yearly right, it's connected.
[00:03:21] Selin Aydın: Yes, we'll get to that, it's in the yellow list.
[00:03:24] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:03:26] Deniz Arı: The amounts, that's clear, I think. Lira and kuruş in full, like "bin iki yüz lira elli kuruş", and if kuruş is zero we don't say "sıfır kuruş".
[00:03:35] Selin Aydın: Yes. And the foreign currencies with cents. Sterlin with pence, um, "peni".
[00:03:40] Ozan Er: Yes, we did that already.
[00:03:42] Burcu Tan: Can I ask something off topic, sorry. Selin, the training on Thursday, is it still on?
[00:03:47] Selin Aydın: Which one? The onboarding group?
[00:03:49] Burcu Tan: The onboarding group, yes. I have two people starting.
[00:03:52] Selin Aydın: I think so. I'll check and write you.
[00:03:54] Burcu Tan: Thanks.
[00:03:56] Ozan Er: One more on the card question. The example card names in "Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, [kart adı] veya [kart adı] diyebilirsiniz." Those are the customer's own cards, max two, right?
[00:04:07] Selin Aydın: Yes. Never a card the customer doesn't have. It would confuse them.
[00:04:11] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:04:12] Deniz Arı: And after the customer picks the card, we go to the debt. No "okay, continuing with your Yıldız card" sentence.
[00:04:18] Selin Aydın: No, that's not needed. The card name is in the first sentence of the reading anyway.
[00:04:23] Deniz Arı: Exactly.
[00:04:24] Selin Aydın: Okay. Let me open the edge cases, so we're ready when Kerem joins. Let me just... the sharing is not... one second.
[00:04:31] Burcu Tan: We see your mail.
[00:04:33] Selin Aydın: Oops. Okay. Now?
[00:04:35] Burcu Tan: Now a white page.
[00:04:37] Selin Aydın: It's loading. The file is big.
[00:04:40] Ozan Er: [inaudible] ...every time.
[00:04:43] Selin Aydın: Sorry?
[00:04:44] Ozan Er: Nothing, I said the same happens to me every time with that tool.
[00:04:48] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Okay. I'll stop sharing until Kerem is in.

[...]

[00:06:41] Kerem Yalçın: ...no, it's fine, the other meeting ran late, sorry. Can everyone hear me?
[00:06:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, loud and clear.
[00:06:45] Burcu Tan: You're a bit echoey Kerem.
[00:06:47] Kerem Yalçın: Hm. Better? I switched to the headset.
[00:06:49] Burcu Tan: Better, yes.
[00:06:51] Selin Aydın: Okay so, um, I'll share my screen. Can you see the document? The statement debt one, the September analysis.
[00:06:58] Ozan Er: Yes, we see it.
[00:07:00] Selin Aydın: Good. So I put the open points in yellow, there are, let me count, eleven? Twelve. We don't have to do all of them today but the edge cases I really want to close because Deniz's team is already building.
[00:07:13] Deniz Arı: Yes, that would help a lot. Most of our questions are in the edge case part anyway. The happy path is quite clear.
[00:07:20] Selin Aydın: Okay. Then let's start with, um, silence. Because that one I wrote quickly and I'm not happy with it.
[00:07:27] Selin Aydın: Right now it says if the customer is silent three times, we go to the main menu.
[00:07:32] Kerem Yalçın: That's what we agreed in September, no?
[00:07:34] Selin Aydın: That's what I wrote, yes.
[00:07:36] Kerem Yalçın: I think it's fine. Main menu, they can choose something else there.
[00:07:40] Ozan Er: Can I ask one thing about the first two? What does the assistant do on the first silence? Because the document only talks about the third.
[00:07:47] Selin Aydın: Ah. Good point. It repeats the question, I'd say.
[00:07:50] Ozan Er: The whole question or a short version?
[00:07:53] Selin Aydın: Short. Like, it asked which card, the customer says nothing, it asks again shorter. Not the whole sentence with the examples.
[00:08:00] Ozan Er: Okay, so silence one, short repeat. Silence two, short repeat. Silence three...
[00:08:05] Kerem Yalçın: Main menu. Let's keep it, we can come back if Burcu has something.
[00:08:09] Burcu Tan: I have something but let me check it first, I'm not sure what the IVR does today exactly. I'll look while you continue.
[00:08:15] Kerem Yalçın: Okay.
[00:08:17] Selin Aydın: Next one. Unclear answer. Or the customer refuses to give the information, like we ask the last four digits and they say "why do you need it", that kind of thing.
[00:08:26] Deniz Arı: For us these are the same branch. The question is asked again and the customer gets three tries. After three, main menu. Is that okay?
[00:08:33] Selin Aydın: Three tries per question, yes. That matches what we do in the IVR.
[00:08:37] Burcu Tan: Yes, three. [inaudible] ...the IVR also counts per menu, not per call.
[00:08:42] Ozan Er: Per question then. And if the customer just asks to hear it again, like "can you repeat the amount", that doesn't count as a try, right?
[00:08:49] Selin Aydın: No, no. Repeating is not a failure. They can ask as many times as they want.
[00:08:53] Ozan Er: Okay. And what does it say when the three tries are gone? Because in the document there's, um, there's a sentence at the bottom of the exit table.
[00:09:00] Selin Aydın: Yes, I wrote "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum."
[00:09:04] Burcu Tan: The IVR says "aktarıyorum". Not "yönlendiriyorum". We had a whole discussion about that two years ago, I don't want to start it again [laughs].
[00:09:11] Kerem Yalçın: And I think it should say why. Not just "I'm transferring you". The customer tried three times, they should hear that we can't help right now.
[00:09:18] Deniz Arı: So something like "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" and then the transfer?
[00:09:22] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Selin, can you write it full?
[00:09:25] Selin Aydın: Typing. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Two sentences.
[00:09:31] Burcu Tan: That's good. That's close to the IVR line.
[00:09:33] Ozan Er: And for the normal end, when the customer says "no, nothing else, thanks"? Same sentence?
[00:09:38] Kerem Yalçın: No, there nothing went wrong. There it's just the transfer.
[00:09:42] Selin Aydın: For the normal end I'd keep "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now. When the call routing project comes we look at all these sentences together anyway.
[00:09:50] Burcu Tan: Fine for me, as long as the failure one says "aktarıyorum".
[00:09:53] Deniz Arı: Noted. Failure after three tries: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Normal end stays as it is in the document.
[00:10:01] Selin Aydın: Yes.
[00:10:03] Kerem Yalçın: Can someone close the door, there's a delivery guy shouting outside here.
[00:10:07] Burcu Tan: That's on your side Kerem [laughs].
[00:10:09] Kerem Yalçın: Ah, yes, sorry. One second. [inaudible]
[00:10:20] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Go on.
[00:10:22] Selin Aydın: Non-Turkish. Customer speaks English or Arabic or German, whatever.
[00:10:27] Deniz Arı: We assume this flow answers only in Turkish?
[00:10:30] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. For now only Turkish. There is an English menu in the IVR, they can go from the main menu.
[00:10:36] Ozan Er: So it doesn't answer the question, it just transfers. What does it say? Turkish, I assume, since the call is Turkish.
[00:10:42] Burcu Tan: Just "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Nothing else. They won't understand a long sentence anyway.
[00:10:47] Selin Aydın: Okay. "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." for non-Turkish. Writing.
[00:10:52] Deniz Arı: Good.
[00:10:54] Selin Aydın: Out of scope next. So in the document I wrote out of scope goes directly to the main menu.
[00:11:00] Deniz Arı: Yes, that's one we wanted to discuss. Ozan, you had the example from the tests.
[00:11:05] Ozan Er: Yes. So we tried it like that and the problem is, the customer asks something small, like, um, "what is my card limit" in the middle of the card selection, and boom, they're in the main menu. They didn't want to leave, they just asked something.
[00:11:18] Kerem Yalçın: Hm.
[00:11:19] Ozan Er: So our proposal: the assistant says it can't help with that, and asks if they want to go to the main menu. If yes, main menu. If they want to continue, back to where they were.
[00:11:28] Kerem Yalçın: I like that. Selin?
[00:11:30] Selin Aydın: Yes, I'm okay. What is the sentence exactly?
[00:11:33] Ozan Er: We had something like "Bu konuda size yardımcı olamıyorum, ana menüye..." uh, I don't remember our wording.
[00:11:39] Kerem Yalçın: Let's make it consistent with the one we just wrote. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" style.
[00:11:45] Selin Aydın: So: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?"
[00:11:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, that sounds natural.
[00:11:53] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Keep it.
[00:11:55] Deniz Arı: And if the answer to that question is unclear? Like they say "hmm, well, I don't know"?
[00:12:00] Selin Aydın: Same as every other question. Ask again, three tries.
[00:12:04] Deniz Arı: And after three, the failure sentence and main menu.
[00:12:07] Selin Aydın: Yes.
[00:12:08] Ozan Er: Good, I'm writing it in our sheet. Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.
[00:12:20] Kerem Yalçın: Wait, payment is not out of scope in that sense. If someone wants to pay, that goes to an agent, we said it in the e-mails.
[00:12:27] Deniz Arı: Yes, yes, payment is separate. Payment and disputes go to an agent. This is only for things that have nothing to do with the statement.
[00:12:33] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Just so it's clear.
[00:12:35] Selin Aydın: Next, the angry customer. In the document: one calming reply, then agent.
[00:12:41] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, that's fine I think. We don't want the bot arguing with an angry customer.
[00:12:46] Deniz Arı: Okay. One calming sentence and then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
[00:12:51] Ozan Er: And insults, we don't answer the insult itself, right? It just stays polite.
[00:12:55] Kerem Yalçın: Never answers the insult. Stays polite, yes.
[00:12:58] Selin Aydın: Okay, that one stays as written then.
[00:13:01] Selin Aydın: Card selection. This is the long one. Mert isn't here but I talked to him yesterday.
[00:13:07] Deniz Arı: Okay, go.
[00:13:09] Selin Aydın: So. The customer has two cards with the same name. Two Yıldız cards, for example. We ask the last four digits.
[00:13:17] Ozan Er: And the question is "Yıldız isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?" That one we have from your document, yes.
[00:13:24] Selin Aydın: Yes. Now, what if the last four are also the same? It's rare but it happens, with renewed cards, or, um, with some business customers.
[00:13:33] Kerem Yalçın: How rare?
[00:13:35] Selin Aydın: I don't have a number. Mert said it exists.
[00:13:38] Kerem Yalçın: Okay.
[00:13:39] Selin Aydın: In the document I wrote: if the last four are the same, ask the full card number.
[00:13:44] Deniz Arı: We'd prefer one step in between. Last six digits. Most people can read six digits off the card without trouble, the full number is sixteen digits, people make mistakes, and saying the full number on the phone, some customers don't like it.
[00:13:56] Elçin Ural: Sorry, I'm joining late. Hello everyone. What are we on?
[00:13:59] Selin Aydın: Hi Elçin. Card selection, two cards same last four digits.
[00:14:03] Elçin Ural: Ah okay. Go on, I'll catch up.
[00:14:05] Deniz Arı: So, last four, then last six, then only if the last six are also the same, the full card number.
[00:14:12] Elçin Ural: From my side it's better if we ask less of the number. Six instead of sixteen, yes, fine.
[00:14:17] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, I'm fine. Selin, sentences?
[00:14:20] Selin Aydın: Um. For the six. "Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?" With the real four digits of course, I just put the ones from the test card.
[00:14:33] Ozan Er: Yes, the digits come from the service. And for the full number?
[00:14:37] Selin Aydın: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
[00:14:43] Ozan Er: Okay. And the digits, when the assistant says "4253" it's digit by digit. Dört, iki, beş, üç. Not "kırk iki elli üç".
[00:14:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR also reads digit by digit.
[00:14:54] Elçin Ural: And it never reads the full number back. Even if the customer says it.
[00:14:58] Deniz Arı: Never. It doesn't repeat what the customer said either, it just goes to the debt of that card.
[00:15:03] Elçin Ural: Good.
[00:15:05] Selin Aydın: Okay. I'll ask Deniz to add the six-digit step as a comment in my document, I'll put it in properly later.
[00:15:11] Deniz Arı: Sure, I'll do it after the call.
[00:15:13] Burcu Tan: Can I go back to silence? I checked.
[00:15:16] Selin Aydın: Yes, go.
[00:15:17] Burcu Tan: So in the IVR today, after the third no-input, we don't send them to the main menu. We hang up. There's a sentence, then disconnect.
[00:15:25] Kerem Yalçın: Really? I thought it went back to the menu.
[00:15:28] Burcu Tan: Only in the main menu itself it loops once. In the sub-menus after three no-inputs, it's goodbye. The logic is, if we can't hear the customer three times, either the line is broken or they left the phone. Sending them to the menu is just more silence.
[00:15:42] Deniz Arı: That makes sense for us too. If there's nobody there, the main menu will also time out.
[00:15:47] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, then let's do the same. Hang up.
[00:15:50] Elçin Ural: The customer should hear why the call is ending. Not just click.
[00:15:54] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR says it. Let me find the exact line... um. It's something about not hearing the caller, I don't have it word for word.
[00:16:01] Ozan Er: For a voice assistant I'd say "alamadığım". Like, the problem is we're not receiving the voice, it's not the customer's fault.
[00:16:07] Selin Aydın: "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." Like that?
[00:16:12] Burcu Tan: Yes, that's fine. Better than ours actually.
[00:16:15] Elçin Ural: Fine for me.
[00:16:16] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Decided. Three silences: first two short repeat, third "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and hang up. Not main menu.
[00:16:25] Deniz Arı: Got it. And we said the first two are just a short repeat of the question.
[00:16:29] Selin Aydın: Yes. I'll fix the document.

[00:16:37] Burcu Tan: Let's leave it. I'll send you what the IVR uses.
[00:16:40] Selin Aydın: Okay. Now, Elçin, since you're here. Currencies. Kerem, this one was for you two.

[00:16:50] Selin Aydın: Yes. So in my table, the sentences for the currencies without debt, I wrote "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", "USD borcunuz bulunmamaktadır" and so on, because it was shorter to type.

[00:17:07] Elçin Ural: No, no abbreviations to the customer. The customer has to hear the currency name in full.
[00:17:12] Kerem Yalçın: Agreed.
[00:17:13] Selin Aydın: So: "Türk Lirası", "Dolar", "Euro", "İngiliz Sterlini".
[00:17:18] Elçin Ural: Yes. TL is Türk Lirası, USD is Dolar, EUR is Euro, GBP is İngiliz Sterlini. Always.
[00:17:24] Deniz Arı: Also in the combined sentence. So "Türk Lirası borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", not "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır".
[00:17:31] Elçin Ural: Yes. Everywhere it speaks.
[00:17:33] Ozan Er: And "Euro" stays "Euro", not "Avro"?
[00:17:36] Elçin Ural: Euro. That's what we use in all customer communication.
[00:17:39] Kerem Yalçın: And İngiliz Sterlini, not just "Sterlin", not "pound".
[00:17:43] Elçin Ural: İngiliz Sterlini, yes.
[00:17:45] Selin Aydın: Okay, I'll change the table. It's fifteen rows, I'll do it tonight.
[00:17:49] Deniz Arı: We'll read them in full on our side anyway, whatever the table says.
[00:17:53] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Still, I'll fix it.
[00:17:56] Burcu Tan: Is someone's mic open? There's typing.
[00:17:59] Ozan Er: Sorry, that's me, I'm taking notes. Muting.
[00:18:03] Selin Aydın: Okay, statement week. The cut-off date change.
[00:18:07] Kerem Yalçın: This is the one with the limit question.
[00:18:09] Selin Aydın: Yes. So in the IVR today... Burcu, you tell.
[00:18:13] Burcu Tan: In the IVR today the customer can change the statement week once a month, and at most three times in a year. Those are the error prompts we have, "ayda bir", "yılda üç". You have them in my prompt sheet.
[00:18:24] Kerem Yalçın: That rule changes with this project. From the product side we decided: once per calendar year. One change per year, per card.
[00:18:33] Burcu Tan: Since when?
[00:18:34] Kerem Yalçın: It's decided for the assistant channel. The IVR prompts will follow, I'll tell your team, but for this flow: once a calendar year.
[00:18:42] Burcu Tan: Okay. Then I need to change my prompts too. Noted.
[00:18:45] Deniz Arı: Calendar year meaning January to December? Not twelve months from the last change?
[00:18:50] Kerem Yalçın: Calendar year. January first resets.
[00:18:53] Deniz Arı: Okay. Then the important thing for us: if the customer already used it this year, we should not offer it.
[00:18:59] Kerem Yalçın: Right. Never offer it to someone who can't do it. That's the worst experience, you offer, they say yes, and then you say "sorry you can't".
[00:19:07] Ozan Er: But we need to know that before the offer. Is there a service that tells us if the right is used? In the contract Mert sent, I didn't see a field for it.
[00:19:15] Selin Aydın: Hm. I don't think there is one now.
[00:19:18] Kerem Yalçın: Let me check with Mert. It should be a small thing to add, a pre-check. Put it as an action on me.
[00:19:24] Deniz Arı: Okay. Kerem, pre-check for the yearly right.
[00:19:27] Ozan Er: And should the assistant tell the customer about the limit? Like before asking the date. "Hesap kesim tarihinizi yılda bir kez değiştirebilirsiniz." Something like that.
[00:19:35] Kerem Yalçın: It can. I wouldn't make it a must.
[00:19:38] Elçin Ural: From compliance, there's no obligation to say it in the call. It's in the card agreement. If it helps the customer decide, fine, it's a good sentence.
[00:19:46] Burcu Tan: I'd say it, people will call back angry otherwise when they want to change again in March [laughs].
[00:19:51] Kerem Yalçın: Then let it be a nice-to-have. Ozan decides where it fits. The rule that matters is: one change per calendar year, and if the right is used, we don't offer the change at all.
[00:20:00] Ozan Er: Okay. And if the customer asks for it anyway, even though we didn't offer?
[00:20:04] Kerem Yalçın: Then explain that the change was already made this year. That's where that sentence is useful.
[00:20:09] Ozan Er: Okay, good.
[00:20:11] Selin Aydın: Next, joint statement. Elçin, this is also yours a bit.
[00:20:15] Elçin Ural: Linked cards?
[00:20:16] Selin Aydın: Yes. If two cards share one statement, a main card and a linked card, changing the week of one changes the other too. In my document, the assistant says it after the customer confirms. Like, "okay, changed, and by the way this also affected your other card".
[00:20:31] Elçin Ural: No. That's too late. The customer has to know before they say yes.
[00:20:35] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, that's not okay, they confirmed without knowing.
[00:20:38] Selin Aydın: Yes, I realised it when I reread it.
[00:20:41] Deniz Arı: So it goes before the confirm question. Before "Onaylıyor musunuz?".
[00:20:45] Elçin Ural: Before the confirm question, yes. Clearly.
[00:20:48] Ozan Er: Sentence? We had a draft, um, "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek."
[00:20:55] Elçin Ural: With the name of the linked card in it?
[00:20:57] Ozan Er: Yes, the card name comes from the service.
[00:21:00] Elçin Ural: Good. That's clear.
[00:21:02] Selin Aydın: "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek." Okay. And the other way, if the customer is calling about the linked card?
[00:21:11] Deniz Arı: Same idea. Before the confirm question we say the change also affects the main card.
[00:21:16] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Whoever calls, before they confirm they hear that the other card moves too.
[00:21:21] Elçin Ural: And they have to say a clear yes. Not "hmm okay maybe".
[00:21:25] Deniz Arı: Yes, we only make the change after a clear yes. If it's unclear we ask once more, clearly.
[00:21:30] Elçin Ural: Good.
[00:21:32] Burcu Tan: Sorry, small thing, the IVR... [inaudible] ...the linked card holder, can they even change it? In the IVR only the main card holder can.
[00:21:40] Kerem Yalçın: In the assistant both can, if they own the card. That was in the scope.
[00:21:44] Burcu Tan: Okay. Just checking.
[00:21:46] Selin Aydın: Okay. Let me see what's left. E-mail. Not much, we did it in the mails. Only the registered address, read it back before sending.
[00:21:54] Deniz Arı: Yes. And one detail: if there's no registered e-mail at all, we don't offer the e-mail. We only offer the week change, if the customer has the right.
[00:22:02] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, logical.
[00:22:04] Ozan Er: And complex addresses, we shorten. Like "m ile başlayan Gmail adresiniz". We don't spell letter by letter.
[00:22:10] Elçin Ural: As long as it's the registered one, I'm fine.
[00:22:13] Selin Aydın: Okay.
[00:22:15] Deniz Arı: Can I go back to the angry customer? I was thinking about it while we did the e-mail.
[00:22:20] Selin Aydın: Sure.
[00:22:21] Deniz Arı: With one calming sentence, in the tests, a lot of customers who are just a bit annoyed, like "ugh, this is the third time I call", they go straight to an agent. And these are people the assistant could actually help in the next sentence.
[00:22:34] Kerem Yalçın: Hm. That's true, annoyed isn't the same as a complaint.
[00:22:38] Elçin Ural: What's the proposal?
[00:22:40] Deniz Arı: Up to three calming replies. If the customer calms down, we continue the flow. If after three they're still complaining, then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." and transfer.
[00:22:50] Burcu Tan: In the call center they also try a few times before escalating. Three is reasonable.
[00:22:55] Elçin Ural: Fine for me, as long as the assistant doesn't argue and doesn't answer insults.
[00:23:00] Ozan Er: No, never. It doesn't react to the insult. Only calming replies, and if the customer asks for an agent directly, we transfer right away, that's separate.
[00:23:07] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Agent request is always immediate. Okay, three calming replies. Selin, can you change it?
[00:23:13] Selin Aydın: So we change what I said ten minutes ago [laughs]. Three calming replies, if the complaint continues, "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." and agent.
[00:23:21] Kerem Yalçın: Yes.
[00:23:22] Deniz Arı: Noted.
[00:23:24] Ozan Er: Can I double check the out-of-scope one, because of the agent topic? If someone asks something out of scope and also sounds angry, which one do we follow?
[00:23:31] Kerem Yalçın: Uh. Good question. If they're complaining, it's the complaint branch. If they just ask something unrelated, the out-of-scope question.
[00:23:38] Selin Aydın: And if they explicitly want an agent, agent. Without trying to convince them.
[00:23:42] Ozan Er: Okay, that's clear enough for us.
[00:23:45] Kerem Yalçın: Guys, I have a hard stop at three, so let's do a quick recap? Deniz?
[00:23:50] Deniz Arı: Sure, quickly, and I'll send it in writing too.
[00:23:53] Deniz Arı: Silence: first two times, short repeat of the question. Third time "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and the call is closed.
[00:24:02] Deniz Arı: Unclear answer or refusal: ask again, three tries per question. After three: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Repeating information doesn't count.
[00:24:12] Deniz Arı: Non-Turkish: "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum."
[00:24:15] Deniz Arı: Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to the flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.
[00:24:26] Deniz Arı: Card selection: same name, last four. Same last four: "Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?" Same last six: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
[00:24:42] Selin Aydın: With the real digits, not 4253.
[00:24:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, of course, from the service.
[00:24:46] Deniz Arı: Angry customer: up to three calming replies, then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum." No reaction to insults.
[00:24:53] Deniz Arı: Currency names always in full, Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini, also in the no-debt sentence.
[00:25:00] Deniz Arı: Statement week: once per calendar year. Not offered if the right is used. Mentioning the limit is optional. Kerem checks the pre-check service with Mert.
[00:25:09] Deniz Arı: Joint statement: before the confirm question, "Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek." For the linked card holder, before the confirm question, that the main card is affected too.
[00:25:21] Deniz Arı: Normal end, nothing else wanted: "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now, to look at again with the routing project.
[00:25:28] Elçin Ural: One correction. For the joint statement, not only "before confirming". Before the question. I want the customer to hear it, and then the question comes.
[00:25:35] Deniz Arı: Yes, that's what I meant. Sentence first, then "Onaylıyor musunuz?".
[00:25:39] Elçin Ural: Okay.
[00:25:40] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Selin, you'll fix the document?
[00:25:43] Selin Aydın: I'll fix what I can by tomorrow. The edge case section I'll redo anyway, it's a mess.
[00:25:51] Deniz Arı: I'll send it, maybe not today, tomorrow or Friday.
[00:25:54] Selin Aydın: Fine.
[00:25:55] Burcu Tan: And I'll send the silence timing from the IVR. And I'll fix my prompts for the yearly limit, but that's for the IVR, not for you.
[00:26:02] Ozan Er: Thanks Burcu.
[00:26:04] Kerem Yalçın: Anything else? The [inaudible] mobile app topic we do next week, not today.
[00:26:09] Selin Aydın: Next week, yes. Ah, and Elçin, mandatory texts, is there anything the assistant must say at the start?
[00:26:15] Elçin Ural: I'm checking. I'll write to you. I don't think so for this flow because the customer is already identified in the IVR, but let me confirm.
[00:26:22] Selin Aydın: Okay, thanks.
[00:26:24] Deniz Arı: One more for us, sorry, thirty seconds. When the debt service doesn't answer, an error, we go to an agent, not main menu. Still okay?
[00:26:31] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Service error, agent. The customer did nothing wrong, they shouldn't land in the menu.
[00:26:36] Deniz Arı: And the sentence from the mails stays, "Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
[00:26:42] Kerem Yalçın: Yes.
[00:26:43] Deniz Arı: Perfect, that's all from us.
[00:26:45] Ozan Er: Oh, last thing, the digits. When the customer says "kırk iki elli üç" for the last four, that's the same as "dört iki beş üç", we just map it, we don't read it back.
[00:26:53] Selin Aydın: Yes, any way they say it.
[00:26:55] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, I really have to go. Thanks everyone, good session.
[00:26:58] Burcu Tan: Bye bye.
[00:26:59] Elçin Ural: Thanks, bye.
[00:27:00] Selin Aydın: Bye. Deniz, Ozan, can you stay one minute?
[00:27:03] Deniz Arı: Sure.
[00:27:05] Selin Aydın: Is it okay for you if the document only catches up next week? I have the quarterly report this week and honestly...
[00:27:11] Deniz Arı: No problem. We have our notes from today.
[00:27:15] Selin Aydın: Thanks. And the six-digit comment, you'll put it?
[00:27:18] Deniz Arı: Yes, right after this.
[00:27:20] Ozan Er: Selin, one question about the test cards, the two Yıldız cards in the test data, do they really share the last four?
[00:27:26] Selin Aydın: I think so, Mert built them for exactly that. Ask him, I'm not a hundred percent sure.
[00:27:31] Ozan Er: Okay, I'll ask.
[00:27:32] Selin Aydın: Okay. Thanks both. Talk Friday.
[00:27:34] Deniz Arı: Thanks, bye.

1	# `out/policy.json`: the canonical extraction
2	
3	Write this file **before** any workflow JSON. It forces one careful reading of the brief, and it is scored field by
4	field against a hand-written answer. Use the brief's own values on the right; the **keys** below are fixed.
5	
6	Every example value on this page is invented ("Example Bank", 2031 dates, `outcome_x`). Never copy an example value:
7	take every value from the brief and the tool API.
8	
9	## Rules for filling it
10	
11	- Every key is present. If the brief is silent, use `null` (or `[]` / `{}`) and say so in `rules.json` with kind
12	  `assumption`.
13	- A value may carry its evidence: put a `"_source"` key next to it inside objects, or a top-level
14	  `"_sources": {"<key>": "<exact quote>"}` map. Quotes are copied from the brief.
15	- Raw briefs (mail threads, memos, code lists): a later or newer statement overrides an earlier one. Use the final
16	  value and record each override in `"_overrides": [{"key": "...", "old": ..., "new": ..., "source": "<quote>"}]`.
17	- Several brief files: they are given in override order. A later file overrides an earlier one.
18	- Enum values (outcomes, reasons, queues, note reasons, codes, product types) are copied **exactly** as the tool API
19	  spells them. When the brief and the tool API disagree on spelling, the tool API wins; record it in `_overrides`.
20	
21	## Keys
22	
23	| Key | Type | Meaning |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| `bank` | string | The bank's name as the agent says it. |
26	| `language` | string | ISO code of the language the agent speaks (`en`, `de`, ...). |
27	| `address` | string | How to address the customer, with `{field}` placeholders from the call variables, e.g. `"{title} {last_name}"`. |
28	| `call_variables` | list[string] | Every variable the documents say a call starts with, and no others. A time variable is included only when the documents name one. Lint treats this list as given. |
29	| `holidays` | list[ISO date] | Every non-business day the brief lists, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, sorted. Convert odd formats (`MON 03.03.31`). |
30	| `bands` | list[object] | One per lateness band, in order: `{"name", "min_days", "max_days", "deadline_business_days", "attempts"}`. |
31	| `attempt1` | string | The brief's rule for the first persuasion proposal, in one sentence of your own words. |
32	| `identity` | object or null | Null when the documents do not ask the assistant to check identity. Otherwise `{"questions": [<field values in order>], "max_wrong": int, "swap_hint": bool}`. `questions` are the tool API's values. `swap_hint` is true when the API returns a hint the documents tell the agent to act on. |
33	| `callback` | object | `{"start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM", "same_day": bool}` plus anything else the brief fixes (e.g. `"days": "today or next business day"`). |
34	| `outcome_map` | object | Canonical key → the brief's own value: `[outcome, reason]` (reason `null` when none), or `[code, null]` when the close tool takes one code. Keys below. |
35	| `queue_map` | object | `{"restructuring": ..., "human": ..., "support": ...}` → the queue value of the transfer tool. `null` for a route the brief does not have. |
36	| `note_map` | object | `{"refused", "hardship", "dispute", "paid", "service_error"}` → the note tool's reason value. Empty `{}` when the brief never uses notes. |
37	| `close_rule` | object | How to close when several products end differently: `{"kind": "first_non_paid"}` or `{"kind": "priority", "order": [<canonical note keys>]}`, or `{"kind": "single"}`. |
38	| `notes_on_restructuring` | string or null | The canonical note key to add before a restructuring transfer, if the brief asks for notes then; `null` if it forbids them. |
39	| `product_types` | object | Canonical product key → `{"enum": <API type value>, "label": "<how the agent names it, {last4} allowed>", "floor_field": "<account field>", "last4_field": "<account field or null>"}`. |
40	| `account_fields` | object | `{"product_id", "type", "past_due", "days_late"}` → the account tool's field names. |
41	| `product_id_format` | string | The id pattern seen in the API or brief, e.g. `"r{n}"`. |
42	| `tools` | object | Per tool, the field names to send (see below), plus `amount_unit` and the callback and close modes. |
43	| `sentences` | object | Sentences the brief fixes, verbatim: `opening`, `promise_confirmation`, `ai`, `scam`, `failed_id`, and any other (e.g. `deceased`). |
44	| `forbidden_before_verify` | list[string] | Words or topics the agent must not say before identity is verified. Empty when the documents have no identity check. |
45	| `multi_product` | bool | True when a customer can have more than one product. |
46	| `max_products` | int | The most products one customer can have. |
47	| `unused_tools` | list[string] | Tools the brief never uses (e.g. notes in a brief that forbids them). Lint stops warning about them. |
48	
49	### Canonical `outcome_map` keys
50	
51	| Key | Situation |
52	|---|---|
53	| `promise` | at least one promise recorded |
54	| `paid` | the customer already paid (every product, in multi-product briefs) |
55	| `tr_restructuring`, `tr_human`, `tr_support` | a transfer to restructuring, to a person, to support |
56	| `np_refused`, `np_hardship`, `np_dispute`, `np_service_error` | verified, no promise: refused, hardship declined, disputed, a write failed |
57	| `nv_failed`, `nv_declined` | identity failed, identity declined |
58	| `nr_callback`, `nr_no_callback`, `nr_wrong_number`, `nr_deceased`, `nr_unclear` | the customer was not reached |
59	
60	A brief may lack some situations: map them to `null`.
61	
62	### `tools` object
63	
64	Keys are the tool API's operationIds, whatever they are called. Each entry has a `role`:
65	`identity`, `account`, `record`, `note`, `callback`, `transfer`, or `close`. Omit a role the brief does not have.
66	The names below are invented.
67	
68	```json
69	{
70	  "check_party": {"role": "identity", "field": "question", "answer": "reply"},
71	  "load_items": {"role": "account"},
72	  "store_agreement": {"role": "record", "product_id": "item_ref", "amount": "amount_minor", "date": "pay_on", "amount_unit": "cents"},
73	  "book_slot": {"role": "callback", "mode": "datetime", "datetime": "slot"},
74	  "end_contact": {"role": "close", "mode": "outcome_reason", "outcome": "outcome", "reason": "detail"},
75	  "hand_off": {"role": "transfer", "queue": "desk"},
76	  "write_note": {"role": "note", "product_id": "item_ref", "reason": "code"}
77	}
78	```
79	
80	- `amount_unit`: `"currency"` (major units, e.g. 412.50) or `"cents"` (integer minor units). On the `record` tool.
81	- `callback` `mode`: `"date_time"` with `"date"` and `"time"` field names, or `"datetime"` with one field name.
82	- `close` `mode`: `"outcome_reason"` with both field names, or `"code"` with `"code": "<field name>"`.
83	
84	## A complete invented example
85	
86	```json
87	{
88	  "bank": "Example Bank",
89	  "language": "en",
90	  "address": "{title} {last_name}",
91	  "call_variables": ["callerRef", "first_name", "last_name", "title", "now"],
92	  "holidays": ["2031-03-14", "2031-04-02"],

| `tools` | object | Per tool, the field names to send (see below), plus `amount_unit` and the callback and close modes. |
| `sentences` | object | Sentences the brief fixes, verbatim: `opening`, `promise_confirmation`, `ai`, `scam`, `failed_id`, and any other (e.g. `deceased`). |
| `forbidden_before_verify` | list[string] | Words or topics the agent must not say before identity is verified. Empty when the documents have no identity check. |
| `multi_product` | bool | True when a customer can have more than one product. |
| `max_products` | int | The most products one customer can have. |
| `unused_tools` | list[string] | Tools the brief never uses (e.g. notes in a brief that forbids them). Lint stops warning about them. |

### Canonical `outcome_map` keys

| Key | Situation |
|---|---|
| `promise` | at least one promise recorded |
| `paid` | the customer already paid (every product, in multi-product briefs) |
| `tr_restructuring`, `tr_human`, `tr_support` | a transfer to restructuring, to a person, to support |
| `np_refused`, `np_hardship`, `np_dispute`, `np_service_error` | verified, no promise: refused, hardship declined, disputed, a write failed |
| `nv_failed`, `nv_declined` | identity failed, identity declined |
| `nr_callback`, `nr_no_callback`, `nr_wrong_number`, `nr_deceased`, `nr_unclear` | the customer was not reached |

A brief may lack some situations: map them to `null`.

### `tools` object

Keys are the tool API's operationIds, whatever they are called. Each entry has a `role`:
`identity`, `account`, `record`, `note`, `callback`, `transfer`, or `close`. Omit a role the brief does not have.
The names below are invented.

```json
{
  "check_party": {"role": "identity", "field": "question", "answer": "reply"},
  "load_items": {"role": "account"},
  "store_agreement": {"role": "record", "product_id": "item_ref", "amount": "amount_minor", "date": "pay_on", "amount_unit": "cents"},
  "book_slot": {"role": "callback", "mode": "datetime", "datetime": "slot"},
  "end_contact": {"role": "close", "mode": "outcome_reason", "outcome": "outcome", "reason": "detail"},
  "hand_off": {"role": "transfer", "queue": "desk"},
  "write_note": {"role": "note", "product_id": "item_ref", "reason": "code"}
}
```

- `amount_unit`: `"currency"` (major units, e.g. 412.50) or `"cents"` (integer minor units). On the `record` tool.
- `callback` `mode`: `"date_time"` with `"date"` and `"time"` field names, or `"datetime"` with one field name.
- `close` `mode`: `"outcome_reason"` with both field names, or `"code"` with `"code": "<field name>"`.

## A complete invented example

```json
{
  "bank": "Example Bank",
  "language": "en",
  "address": "{title} {last_name}",
  "call_variables": ["callerRef", "first_name", "last_name", "title", "now"],
  "holidays": ["2031-03-14", "2031-04-02"],
  "bands": [
    {"name": "first", "min_days": 1, "max_days": 20, "deadline_business_days": 5, "attempts": 1},
    {"name": "second", "min_days": 21, "max_days": 60, "deadline_business_days": 3, "attempts": 2}
  ],
  "attempt1": "the last business day of the current week, or of next week when today is that day; never after the deadline",
  "identity": {"questions": ["member_code", "birth_month"], "max_wrong": 2, "swap_hint": false},
  "callback": {"start": "09:00", "end": "17:00", "same_day": true, "days": "today or the next business day"},
  "outcome_map": {
    "promise": ["outcome_x", null], "paid": ["outcome_v", null],
    "tr_restructuring": ["outcome_y", "detail_r"], "tr_human": ["outcome_y", "detail_a"], "tr_support": ["outcome_y", "detail_b"],
    "np_refused": ["outcome_u", "detail_f"], "np_hardship": ["outcome_u", "detail_g"], "np_dispute": ["outcome_u", "detail_h"],
    "np_service_error": ["outcome_u", "detail_c"],
    "nv_failed": ["outcome_z", "detail_a"], "nv_declined": ["outcome_z", "detail_e"],
    "nr_callback": ["outcome_w", "detail_a"], "nr_no_callback": ["outcome_w", "detail_d"],
    "nr_wrong_number": ["outcome_w", "detail_b"], "nr_deceased": null, "nr_unclear": ["outcome_w", "detail_c"]
  },
  "queue_map": {"restructuring": null, "human": "desk_x", "support": "desk_y"},
  "note_map": {"refused": "note_x", "hardship": "note_z", "dispute": "note_w", "paid": "note_y", "service_error": "note_v"},
  "close_rule": {"kind": "priority", "order": ["dispute", "hardship", "refused", "service_error"]},
  "notes_on_restructuring": null,
  "product_types": {
    "a": {"enum": "kind_a", "label": "item ending {last4}", "floor_field": "floor_amount", "last4_field": "ending"},
    "b": {"enum": "kind_b", "label": "second item", "floor_field": "floor_amount", "last4_field": null}
  },
  "account_fields": {"product_id": "item_ref", "type": "kind", "past_due": "overdue", "days_late": "days_over"},
  "product_id_format": "r{n}",
  "tools": {
    "check_party": {"role": "identity", "field": "question", "answer": "reply"},
    "load_items": {"role": "account"},
    "store_agreement": {"role": "record", "product_id": "item_ref", "amount": "amount_minor", "date": "pay_on", "amount_unit": "cents"},
    "book_slot": {"role": "callback", "mode": "datetime", "datetime": "slot"},
    "end_contact": {"role": "close", "mode": "outcome_reason", "outcome": "outcome", "reason": "detail"},
    "hand_off": {"role": "transfer", "queue": "desk"},
    "write_note": {"role": "note", "product_id": "item_ref", "reason": "code"}
  },
  "sentences": {
    "opening": "the automated assistant of Example Bank; the call is recorded",
    "promise_confirmation": "You will get a letter about this promise.",
    "ai": "Example Bank's automated assistant",
    "scam": "check the call on the number printed on your member card",
    "failed_id": "visit a branch"
  },
  "forbidden_before_verify": ["money", "item", "late"],
  "multi_product": true,
  "max_products": 2,
  "unused_tools": [],
  "_overrides": [{"key": "callback.end", "old": "18:00", "new": "17:00", "source": "from Monday the line closes at 17:00"}]
}
```

1	# Tools and code
2	
3	This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.
4	
5	Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.
6	
7	## Tool function shape
8	
9	Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "type": "function",
14	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
15	  "function": {
16	    "name": "lookup_order",
17	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
18	    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
19	    "parameters": {
20	      "type": "object",
21	      "properties": {
22	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
23	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
24	        "headers": {
25	          "type": "object",
26	          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
27	        },
28	        "body": {
29	          "type": "object",
30	          "properties": {
31	            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
32	            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
33	          },
34	          "required": ["order_number"]
35	        }
36	      }
37	    }
38	  },
39	  "response_mapping": [
40	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
41	  ]
42	}
43	```
44	
45	| Field | Meaning |
46	|---|---|
47	| `type` | Always `"function"` |
48	| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
49	| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
50	| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
51	| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
52	| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
53	| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
54	| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
55	| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
56	| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
57	| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
58	| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |
59	
60	| Handler | Runs |
61	|---|---|
62	| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
63	| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
64	| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |
65	
66	Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.
67	
68	`api_call` parameters:
69	
70	| Parameter | Meaning |
71	|---|---|
72	| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
73	| `method` | HTTP method |
74	| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
75	| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
76	| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |
77	
78	## How a parameter gets its value
79	
80	One key decides, per parameter: `default`.
81	
82	| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
85	| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
86	| no `default` | The model | Yes |
87	| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |
88	
89	Rules:
90	
91	- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
92	- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
93	- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.
94	
95	The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.
96	
97	Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.
98	
99	Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.
100	
101	### `api_call` body field rules
102	
103	- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
104	- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
105	- Give each leaf its own `default`.
106	- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
107	- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.
108	
109	A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.
110	
111	### When a baked variable has no value
112	
113	| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
116	| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |
117	
118	Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.
119	
120	### Constrain model-filled parameters
121	
122	When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.
123	
124	- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
125	- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
126	- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.
127	
128	```json
129	{
130	  "type": "object",
131	  "properties": {
132	    "queue": {
133	      "type": "string",
134	      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
135	      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
136	      "default": "{{queue}}"
137	    }
138	  },
139	  "required": ["queue"]
140	}
141	```
142	
143	## `pre_actions` versus `tools`
144	
145	The placement decides who fires the call.
146	
147	| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
150	| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
151	| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |
152	
153	The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.
154	
155	**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.
156	
157	**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.
158	
159	Differences in behaviour:
160	
161	| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
164	| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
165	| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
166	| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
167	| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |
168	
169	To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.
170	
171	### A `pre_actions` node
172	
173	```json
174	{
175	  "name": "fetch_order",
176	  "node_type": "api_request",
177	  "passthrough": true,

# Tools and code

This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.

Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.

## Tool function shape

Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
  "function": {
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "headers": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
        },
        "body": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
          },
          "required": ["order_number"]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"function"` |
| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |

| Handler | Runs |
|---|---|
| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

### Constrain model-filled parameters

When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.

- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "queue": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
      "default": "{{queue}}"
    }
  },
  "required": ["queue"]
}
```

## `pre_actions` versus `tools`

The placement decides who fires the call.

| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |

The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.

**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.

**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.

Differences in behaviour:

| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
|---|---|---|
| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |

To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.

### A `pre_actions` node

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_order",
  "node_type": "api_request",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
      "function": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "description": "Get the order.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.

### Tool descriptions

In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.

- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."

A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."

```json

    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
```

|---|---|

| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |

487	
488	A global node is an interrupt handler. It can fire from any node. It is checked only after the current node's own transitions found no match.

### Global nodes

A global node is an interrupt handler. It can fire from any node. It is checked only after the current node's own transitions found no match.

A global node has the same fields as a normal node, plus:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `condition` | When the global node activates. Same format as a transition condition |
| `description` | Purpose of the node |
| `excluded_nodes` | Array of node keys where it must not fire |
| `is_tool_call` | Offer the global node to the dialogue model as a tool, not as a per-turn check |

`__previous__` as a `target_node` or as `passthrough_default_transition` returns to the node that was interrupted.

```json
    "off_topic": {
      "name": "off_topic",
```

612

614

626	      "handler": "__function__:end_call",
627	      "parameters": {
628	        "type": "object",
629	        "properties": {

631	          "spoken_message": { "type": "string", "default": "Thank you for calling. Goodbye." }
632	        }
633	      }
634	    }
635	  }
636	}
637	```
638

640	|---|---|
641	| `message_mode` | `custom`: say `spoken_message`. `llm`: the model writes the farewell from `llm_prompt`. `none`: hang up without a farewell |
642	| `spoken_message` | The fixed farewell for `custom`. `{{var}}` works |
643	| `llm_prompt` | The instruction for `llm` |
644	| `interruptible` | `true` opens a short window after the farewell in which the user can still speak. Default: hang up as soon as the agent stops speaking |
645	| `trigger_timeout` | Length of that window in seconds |
646	| `trigger_pattern_both` | Farewell phrases, separated by `\|`, that do not cancel the close. Anything else the user says in the window cancels the close and returns the turn to the agent |
647

649	
650	- **The farewell comes from the terminal, not from `on_enter`.** A node with an `on_enter` line and `message_mode: "none"` hangs up silently. Put the sentence in `spoken_message` and set `on_enter` to `{"type": "silent"}`.

654	- If you set `interruptible`, also set `trigger_pattern_both`. Without a phrase list every polite reply cancels the hang-up. The window is timed on a wall clock and a chat simulation cannot measure it.

Use extraction for user speech. For API responses use `response_mapping` (tools-and-code.md). It is deterministic and needs no model call.

## End-call nodes

An `end_call` node hangs up. It has a `terminal` object and no outgoing transitions.

```json
{
  "name": "goodbye",
  "node_type": "end_call",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "disable_inactivity_monitor": true,
  "transitions": [],
  "terminal": {
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "closing_end",
      "handler": "__function__:end_call",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "message_mode": { "type": "string", "default": "custom" },
          "spoken_message": { "type": "string", "default": "Thank you for calling. Goodbye." }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `message_mode` | `custom`: say `spoken_message`. `llm`: the model writes the farewell from `llm_prompt`. `none`: hang up without a farewell |
| `spoken_message` | The fixed farewell for `custom`. `{{var}}` works |
| `llm_prompt` | The instruction for `llm` |
| `interruptible` | `true` opens a short window after the farewell in which the user can still speak. Default: hang up as soon as the agent stops speaking |
| `trigger_timeout` | Length of that window in seconds |
| `trigger_pattern_both` | Farewell phrases, separated by `\|`, that do not cancel the close. Anything else the user says in the window cancels the close and returns the turn to the agent |

Rules:

- **The farewell comes from the terminal, not from `on_enter`.** A node with an `on_enter` line and `message_mode: "none"` hangs up silently. Put the sentence in `spoken_message` and set `on_enter` to `{"type": "silent"}`.
- Set `disable_inactivity_monitor` to `true` and `transitions` to `[]`.
- **The call's `endedReason` is the terminal's `function.name`.** The node name does not affect it. Pick a name that describes the outcome.
- Use several end-call nodes with different farewells and function names when outcomes differ.
- If you set `interruptible`, also set `trigger_pattern_both`. Without a phrase list every polite reply cancels the hang-up. The window is timed on a wall clock and a chat simulation cannot measure it.

Verified in a working builder: `message_mode: "none"` with a silent `on_enter` ends the call when the node is reached. The agent says its goodbye in the previous conversation node.

6

8	limit (attempts, wrong answers, windows, minimums), each fixed sentence the brief requires at a turn. 10 to 25 tests
9	are typical. They are cheap; a missed route is expensive.

12

18	   "start_node": "offer",

20	                 "offer_ref": "r1", "offer_item": "0", "offer_step": "0"},
21	   "messages": [{"role": "assistant", "text": "For your item ending 1234, could you pay 412.50 by Wednesday 12 March?"},
22	                {"role": "user", "text": "No, I can't do that."}],
23	   "expect": "The agent does not repeat the proposal and does not record a promise.",
24	   "checks": [{"var": "offer_answer", "equals": "refused"}, {"node": "next_offer"},
25	              {"tool": "store_record", "absent": true}]},
26	
27	  {"name": "last wrong answer ends the check", "rule": "R14",
28	   "start_node": "check",
29	   "variables": {"wrong_total": "1"},
30	   "messages": [{"role": "assistant", "text": "What is your six-digit member code?"},
31	                {"role": "user", "text": "One two three four five six."}],
32	   "mock": {"check_party": {"ok": true, "verified": false, "tries_left": 0}},
33	   "expect": "The agent ends the check without naming any item or amount.",
34	   "checks": [{"tool": "check_party", "body": {"question": "member_code"}}, {"tool": "load_items", "absent": true}]}
35	]
36	```
37	
38	| Field | Meaning |
39	|---|---|
40	| `name` | unique, says what is checked |
41	| `rule` | the `rules.json` id the test covers |
42	| `start_node` | the node the agent is in when the customer speaks (a node id of your workflow) |
43	| `variables` | the variable table at that moment: everything the node's prompt and conditions read (facts, flags, counters) |

52	check, a record tool, or any fixed tool list. A policy with no identity check gets no identity template. Templates
53	that can appear, when the policy has the matching fact, are: a robot question, a scam question, callbacks inside and
54	outside the window, wrong number, deceased, the last wrong identity answer, a declined identity check, a person

- **Single card:** the agent finds the card, reads the debt and the due date, and makes the offer, without asking the caller anything.

- **Escalations:** payment requests, agent requests, disputes and service failures go to an agent, with the quoted sentences in the documents' Turkish.

- **Code check:** I ran only the debt-reading code, against example 1's data. It produced the expected Turkish reading, with amounts in words, full currency names and the last four digits read one by one. I did not run the other hooks.
